title: Make interrupted jobs retryable and picked up by drain
summary: An interrupted job (dispatched, no live process, no closing record) is accepted by `athena retry`, and `athena drain` lists it as work and retries it. The audience is the user running athena where machines restart; today they must close the job by hand and re-ask.

defaults_applied.how: New unit and CLI tests for retry and drain on interrupted jobs; cargo test, clippy and fmt --check pass.
Criteria run retry and drain against an interrupted job and check the resulting proposal and queue.
Fix retry eligibility and drain queue selection, not just the one job.
Update hints, module docs and CHANGELOG for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Interrupted means JobState::Dispatched with no process in the registry (status.rs already derives this); a running job stays refused.
Retrying an interrupted job does not require a verification or outcome record; the carried text is the original request plus a note that the run was interrupted (no failure reason).
The retry check is in earlier_attempt in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, which currently bails on anything but rejected or failed and on missing verification/outcome.
Drain treats interrupted jobs on its own channel as work and retries them; other channels are left alone.
The old interrupted job may be left as is or closed by the retry; the producer picks the least surprising option consistent with existing retry behavior and documents it.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test (cargo test) makes a job dispatched with no live process, runs retry on it, and gets a proposal whose request is 'try again on <id>' carrying the original request, not the error 'only a rejected or failed job can be tried again'.
A test (cargo test) shows a job whose process is still running is refused by retry with a clear message saying it is running.
A drain test (cargo test) with an interrupted job on the drained channel shows it listed as work and retried, with no empty-queue report; an interrupted job on another channel is left alone.
The `athena status` next-step hint for interrupted jobs (status.rs) and the run.rs interrupted message name retry as a way to resume, alongside close.
drain.rs module docs and CHANGELOG.md describe interrupted jobs being retryable and drained.
cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check all pass.

out_of_scope: Changing how plan reads requests or the queued/proposed state (the other half of job mx7e).
Preventing interruptions or automatically detecting container restarts.
Changing retry behavior for rejected or failed jobs.
departures: Touches retry eligibility plus drain selection and tests across core and CLI, so slightly above the reference cost.
